propositions: Rebar must support safe credential passage across eight providers (Bedrock, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gerrit, GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, Jira) and eight deployment contexts without a universal secret broker or credential store that would weaken provider-native refresh, workload identity, and rotation.

Static credentials must rotate by restart or redeploy; long-running processes do not poll, refresh, or watch secret files, and missing credentials before restart cause fail-closed auth failures without fallback.

Deployment resolves external secret stores (SSM, vaults, or files) before process startup and supplies credentials only to their owning adapter as either a file path (REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH) or multiline environment value; Rebar consumes provider-native credential/session/identity capabilities and materializes unavoidable static values only inside provider-specific non-serializable containers with comparison/hash/repr exclusion.

Trusted same-capability child processes inherit ambient environment for compatibility; Rebar removes only exact sibling adapter secret names and overlays materialized secrets only for their owning child without mutating global os.environ.

Operation snapshots are structurally non-secret; provider-specific static-auth containers use Pydantic SecretStr/SecretBytes for defense-in-depth masking but remain non-serializable and excluded from caches, fingerprints, and MCP/CLI surfaces.

Per-job operation-certificate signing accepts deployment-supplied key material at startup, validates before enqueue, copies to a process-owned 0700-directory/0600-file runtime copy, and binds signer/principal/push policy context-locally with no application-owned SSM retrieval, keyring adapter, or built-in cloud-secret manager.
